name: SDF meshes and caves
what: Model smooth organic shapes in code as signed distance fields (spheres, ellipsoids, round cones, tubes along curves, boxes, cylinders; smooth union, subtract, intersect, shells, relief) and mesh them at load time with surface nets: vertices projected onto the exact surface, analytic normals, baked cavity occlusion. Plus seeded 3D caves (tubes of open space, domain-warped and roughened) meshed in 24 m chunks by a Web Worker pool and streamed around the player, with collision against the same field.
use_when: the game needs organic or rounded 3D shapes (creatures, bones, helmets, rocks, blobby props) built in code instead of modelled, or true 3D caves and tunnels that the player moves through

third_party.what: Smooth min/max, ellipsoid and round cone distance formulas
third_party.author: Inigo Quilez

third_party.what: three.js (npm, for geometry.js, streamer.js and the demo)
third_party.author: three.js authors

good_for: creatures, characters, bones, helmets and props made of blended primitives; rocks and boulders; one-off sculpted pieces; cut-away dioramas; underwater or underground games with real 3D caves, overhangs and shafts; anything that must look smooth without any model files
not_for: meshing every frame (it is a load-time tool: 0.1-1 s per shape); hard-edged architecture (use boxes); big open landscapes seen from the air (use a heightmap); skinned animation (it makes static meshes; skin them yourself)
how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs meticulai-sdf-meshes, then import from vendor/meticulai-sdf-meshes/src/index.js (no three.js needed) and geometry.js / streamer.js (three.js); see HOW-TO-USE.md
